message:
We’ll design for about 200 members, shared email addresses, offline returns and inspection before re-lending, recording roughly $80/month for running costs separately from build costs, with currency still open. Let’s add separate member identities, a device-held return queue and an inspection hold; these need custom implementation, and Azure costs remain unverified.

**Will volunteers record offline returns on library-owned devices or personal phones?** This changes how we protect member information stored offline—for example, “one shared library tablet”; “not sure” is fine.

followUp.question: Will volunteers record offline returns on library-owned devices or personal phones?
followUp.why: Device ownership changes how we protect member information stored offline and manage shared access.
followUp.example: One shared library tablet; volunteers' personal phones; or not sure.

proposal.title: Support shared emails, offline returns and inspection holds
proposal.body: Preserve all existing components, positions and connections. Extend the browser application with durable offline return capture and server reconciliation; add an inspection gate before equipment becomes available. Propose distinct member identities independent of email addresses. Device ownership, admission rules and budget currency remain unresolved. Approximately 200 members is a population input, not request volume. Existing Azure placement remains proposed; custom application, integration and infrastructure implementation gaps remain open.

next.name: Community equipment library
next.requirements: I run a community equipment library. I need a website where members reserve tools, volunteers check them out and back in, and overdue reminders go by email. We already have a public website and a spreadsheet of members. We are in Australia. Please help me build this on Azure.

data.label: Existing public website
data.description: Existing externally managed website, preserved outside provisioning scope. Propose adding a link to the borrowing application; hosting platform and change ownership remain unknown.

data.label: Existing member spreadsheet
data.description: Existing member records; file platform, fields and permissions are unknown. Propose an operator-reviewed initial import with validation and duplicate detection, rather than assuming continuous spreadsheet synchronization. Membership authority after import remains to be agreed.

data.label: Members and volunteers
data.description: About 200 members plus volunteers use existing browsers outside provisioning scope. Some members share email addresses; each member requires a distinct member record, and email alone must not establish identity or account ownership. Volunteers can hold both roles. Propose enabling offline returns only after online volunteer sign-in on an enrolled device. Device ownership and shared-device use remain unresolved; local data protection, sign-out cleanup and recovery require implementation.

data.label: Equipment borrowing website
data.description: Proposed Azure App Service hosts the browser interface and server API for inventory, reservations, checkout/return, reviewed member import and server-side permissions. Serve an installable web application that, after initial online setup, durably queues minimal return events in browser IndexedDB during outages, visibly marks them pending synchronization and retains them until server acknowledgement. Events carry stable operation IDs, loan/tool references and volunteer attribution. On reconnect, reauthorize, deduplicate and reconcile against current loan state; rejected or conflicting events remain visible for authorized resolution. Offline capture cannot confirm server acceptance or make equipment available. Accepted returns enter awaiting-inspection state; only an authorized recorded inspection can release equipment for borrowing. Shared emails must not merge members or grant access to another member's records. SQL transactions prevent conflicting reservations and enforce inspection holds at reservation and checkout. A scheduled WebJob processes a durable SQL reminder outbox with bounded retries and duplicate suppression. Recheck loan state before email; returns not yet synchronized remain unknown to the server. Loan rules and reminder timing remain open. Custom source, offline synchronization, identity integration, deployment and tests are required; no generated workload or supplied image exists. Australia East remains proposed, with availability and residency unverified. Approximately 200 members and roughly $80/month running budget recorded; currency and feasibility remain unresolved.

data.label: Members, equipment and loans
data.description: Proposed Azure SQL Database stores distinct member IDs, login mappings, nonunique contact email addresses, volunteer permissions, equipment, reservations, loan history, inspection records, audit events and reminder outbox. Store return operation IDs and reconciliation outcomes transactionally so replay cannot duplicate or reverse a completed return. Accepted returns move equipment to awaiting inspection; reservations and checkout require an eligible inspected state. Record volunteer identity, device-reported event time and server receipt time separately; client timestamps cannot authorize changes. Keep rejected synchronization events visible for resolution. Application access uses narrowly scoped managed identity; browsers have no direct database access. Reviewed member import, transactional invariants, backup/restore, retention and operating ownership require implementation. Australia East remains proposed and unverified.

data.label: Member and volunteer sign-in
data.description: Proposed Microsoft Entra External ID handles member-facing sign-in. The application maps a verified identity subject to approved membership records; contact email is nonunique and must never automatically link accounts or authorize access. Propose individual sign-in identifiers independent of shared email addresses, with explicitly reviewed account recovery and any delegated household access. Exact External ID sign-in and recovery support requires validation before committing to a configuration. Successful sign-in does not grant volunteer permissions. Offline capture uses a previously authorized local session; synchronization requires fresh server authorization, with rejection and recovery visible to the volunteer. Admission model, tenant geography and device policy remain open. Custom integration is required.

data.label: Overdue reminder email
data.description: Proposed Azure Communication Services Email sends overdue reminders requested by the application worker. Requires verified sender/domain, supported data location and delivery-status handling. Exact provisioning resources and API authorization require engineering. Provider acceptance is distinct from inbox delivery; uncertain sends require reconciliation before retry. No service availability or Australian-only processing is established.

edges.label: HTTPS; offline return queue on device, authorized sync after reconnect — custom
Managed-identity SQL: bookings, deduplicated returns, inspection holds — to implement
OpenID Connect; distinct identity-to-member mapping, shared contact emails — to implement
Email send API and delivery status — to implement

requirementDrafts.rationale: An internet outage must not prevent return capture or cause silent loss, duplicate processing or premature equipment availability. Browser storage can be cleared or a device lost, so storage persistence and recovery limits require explicit implementation and testing.
requirementDrafts.basis: “Volunteers must be able to record returns even when the internet drops”
requirementDrafts.statement: Volunteers can capture returns during an internet outage after initial online setup. Proposed behavior: persist minimal return events locally across application restarts, display pending synchronization, retry with stable operation IDs, reauthorize and deduplicate on reconnect, and retain rejected/conflicting events for resolution. Local capture must not imply server acceptance or release equipment for borrowing.

requirementDrafts.rationale: The running budget constrains the whole Azure composition; no current pricing or usage evidence establishes affordability. Keeping build costs separate avoids presenting development expenditure as a cloud charge.
requirementDrafts.basis: “We have about 200 members and a budget around $80 a month.”
requirementDrafts.statement: Proposed planning constraint: assess recurring Azure hosting, database, identity, email and operational charges against roughly $80 per month for approximately 200 members. Currency, traffic and budget flexibility remain open; one-off development costs must be estimated separately. Member count must not be treated as monthly request volume.

requirementUpdates.rationale: Shared contact addresses cannot safely identify a unique member or establish permission to view another person's borrowing records. Membership admission remains unresolved.
requirementUpdates.statement: Authenticate users and enforce member/volunteer permissions on the server. Maintain distinct member records when email addresses are shared; never automatically merge accounts or grant access based on email alone. Proposed sign-in mapping uses verified identity subjects with reviewed recovery and any delegated access. Preserve reviewed member import; admission remains open.
requirementUpdates.sourceText: Some members share an email address.

requirementUpdates.rationale: A return and readiness for borrowing are different states; the server must enforce the inspection gate even when returns arrive late or repeatedly after an outage.
requirementUpdates.statement: Members can reserve eligible equipment; volunteers can record checkout and return against durable loan records, including offline return capture with later reconciliation. Returned equipment remains unavailable for borrowing until an authorized inspection releases it. Proposed acceptance rejects conflicting reservations and safely handles repeated or delayed submissions without bypassing the inspection hold.
requirementUpdates.sourceText: Volunteers must be able to record returns even when the internet drops, and a returned tool needs inspection before anyone can borrow it again.

skills.name: Architecture composition and engineering judgment
skills.summary: Choose and compose blocks through responsibility, contracts, state, identity, failure modes and trade-offs; verify the complete system.
skills.source: AtMem AI Architect reviewed specialist guidance

skills.name: AI architecture and discovery
skills.summary: Clarify outcome, users, existing systems, data ownership and constraints. Evolve the diagram incrementally. Derive functional requirements and propose measurable quality targets as assumptions needing confirmation. Compare clouds against the actual requirements; do not assume an enterprise identity provider or a vendor. Keep proposed and accepted decisions distinct.
skills.source: AtMem AI Architect reviewed specialist guidance

skills.name: Security and reliability
skills.summary: Check data classification, residency, access boundaries, encryption choices, approval of automated actions, reliability and recovery. A drawn control is not enforcement evidence. Explain missing controls and tests. Propose requirements from the components and paths; mark default targets as suggestions, never existing company policy.
skills.source: AtMem AI Architect reviewed specialist guidance

skills.name: FinOps and progressive estimation
skills.summary: Populate a bill of resources from the diagram. Separate monthly cloud charges from one-off build effort. Use pricing.lookup for supported current list pricing, and project.read for usage. Ask the largest missing usage/model/region question. Input and output tokens, storage, requests, duration, networking and observability can have separate charges. Never invent prices or effort. Options cost scores are qualitative judgements, not price quotes.
skills.source: AtMem AI Architect reviewed specialist guidance

skills.name: Azure architecture guidance
skills.summary: Check Microsoft 365/Entra integration only when relevant to the user. Match model, retrieval, data and runtime services to requirements. Evaluate redundancy, regional availability, identity and recovery separately. The pinned Azure reliability reference specifically covers Functions and App Service; do not extend its validation claims to other services.
